core.title: Prefix a themed product capability's produced URNs with the product capability theme
core.given: A product capability declares a theme and produces artifacts, contracts, or telemetry identities (newly authored or already existing, declared in any location).
core.when: The planner authors, edits, validates, or reviews that product capability or any of its produced identities; theme or URN edits are examples, not the only trigger.
core.then: Make the leading theme segment of every produced artifact, contract, and telemetry URN equal the product capability's declared theme.
avoid: Reusing another theme's prefix for a produced URN because the artifact feels related to that domain.
Treating this namespace check as a statement about runtime module ownership, agent roles, or domain vocabulary.
Changing the product capability's theme just to make a mismatched URN pass instead of fixing the URN namespace.
unless: The product capability declares no theme: it is not subject to this cross-field predicate.
core.why: The theme token namespaces produced URNs; this is namespace consistency only, so a mismatched prefix breaks the identity namespace without implying anything about ownership, roles, or vocabulary.
evidence: The stack's static convention check reports no themed product capability whose produced artifact, contract, or telemetry URN theme prefix differs from the product capability theme.
Reviewer can compare the product capability's theme field with the first theme segment of each produced URN.
verification: A static convention check compares the leading theme segment of each produced artifact, contract, and telemetry identity URN with the product capability's declared theme; a differing prefix is the reported violation. Applicability is the presence of a declared theme plus at least one produced identity; the mismatched prefix is the violation outcome, not an activation precondition.

Scope: produced artifact, contract, and telemetry identity URNs only, wherever declared, with no file kind or location restriction; product capabilities with no declared theme are skipped; URNs the product capability consumes but does not produce are out of scope. All themed product capabilities are checked, not only those touched by the current change, including pre-existing ones.

The check requires an observer that reads every product capability's declared theme and the URNs of all identities it produces, wherever those are declared (observability: needs a new observer where the stack has none).

values: a product capability declares a theme and produces at least one artifact, contract, or telemetry identity URN

fires: Authoring, editing, validating, or reviewing any product capability that declares a theme and produces artifacts, contracts, or telemetry identities, wherever its produced identities are declared, even if the current edit touched neither the theme nor the URNs.
Adding a produced artifact, contract, or telemetry URN to a themed product capability.
Changing a product capability's declared theme while it already produces identities.
doesNotFire: A product capability that declares no theme.
Questions of runtime module ownership, agent roles, or domain vocabulary — this rule only checks namespace prefixes.
URNs the product capability consumes but does not produce.

bunOnly.reason: Names this rule's concrete validator implementation of the ATDD-Bun realization; the core names the check generically, because detector/validator/finding ids of a single rule are realization details, not profile data.
The finding/term id of this one rule in the ATDD-Bun realization is a realization detail; its neutral definition (the leading theme segment of a produced URN) is carried in core:verification.

classification.note: Already stack-neutral: product capability, theme, and produced identity URNs are shared ATDD planning-model concepts, with no location restriction.
'The planner' is the ATDD agent role, not a stack role; text carries over verbatim.
The single obligation is stack-neutral; the 'leading theme segment' notion is defined by the rule itself, not by stack data.
The only exception, carried verbatim; also reflected in the check's skip behavior in core:verification.
Rationale is about the identity namespace, stack-neutral.
Neutral restatement ('the stack's static convention check') goes to the core; the concrete validator id planner.static.validators.bun is a realization detail kept in bunOnly.
Human review evidence, stack-neutral, carried verbatim.
The neutral definition (leading theme segment must equal the product capability theme) is in core:verification; the term id urn_theme_prefix is a realization detail kept in bunOnly.

Check scope: produced artifact/contract/telemetry URNs only, wherever declared, no location restriction, themed product capabilities without a theme skipped, all themed product capabilities checked not only changed ones; carried into the core's verification scope entry.
Per-rule severity and disposition are not profile keys; 'Severity 3; disposition strict' goes to core:verification verbatim.

Fact, values, and observability (needs_new_observer) carried into the core; the note's substantive content (applicability not violation, observer must read every product capability's theme and all produced URNs wherever declared, applies to pre-existing product capabilities) is carried in core:verification.

neutralityNotes: The rule is written entirely in the shared ATDD planning-model vocabulary (product capability, theme, produced artifact/contract/telemetry identity URNs), which the profile vocabulary itself treats as cross-stack (e.g. layout.capability_dir exists as a profile key), so given/when/then/avoid/unless/why and the activation lists carry over verbatim. The rule deliberately imposes no file-kind or location restriction ('wherever those are declared'), and bun.json states no concrete paths, URN shapes, or theme-declaration syntax, so the core needs no structural profile data: profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The only Bun-specific content is the validator implementation id in evidence[0] and the finding term id urn_theme_prefix in verifier_detail[0], both kept in bunOnly; per-rule severity and disposition are carried in core:verification per the closed-vocabulary rules.
